description: Composite fractography figure of six panels arranged in two rows, comparing the impact fracture surfaces of the 0Al steel (top row: a, b, c) and the 1.3Al steel (bottom row: d, e, f). (a) and (d) are macroscopic photographs of the whole fracture surface, each with a 1 mm scale bar; a white line traces the outer/shear-lip boundary and a white arrow labelled "b, c" in (a) and "e, f" in (d) marks the central region examined at higher magnification. (b) and (e) are SEM micrographs with 100 µm scale bars of the fibrous central zone: yellow dashed circles enclose primary and merged dimples, green arrows mark elongated voids, and (e) carries the yellow label "Dimples growing"; the dimples in (e) are visibly larger, deeper and more numerous than in (b). (c) and (f) are higher-magnification SEM micrographs (25 µm scale bars) in which blue dashed outlines mark flat quasi-cleavage facets — explicitly labelled "Quasi-cleavage" in (c) — and a green arrow marks a tearing ridge. Together the panels show that both steels fail by ductile void growth and coalescence combined with quasi-cleavage, and that the 1.3Al steel fractures with a coarser, denser dimple population.

observations.observation: The figure contains six panels in two rows: macroscopic fracture surfaces (a) and (d) with 1 mm scale bars, SEM micrographs (b) and (e) with 100 µm scale bars, and SEM micrographs (c) and (f) with 25 µm scale bars.

In (a) and (d) a white line traces the outer boundary of the fracture surface and a white arrow labelled "b, c" (in a) and "e, f" (in d) marks the central region that is magnified in the following panels.
Panel (b) shows a fully dimpled ductile fracture surface in which yellow dashed circles enclose large primary/merged dimples and green arrows point to elongated voids.
Panel (c) contains blue dashed outlines explicitly labelled "Quasi-cleavage", together with finer secondary dimples, at a 25 µm scale bar.
Panel (e) carries the yellow printed label "Dimples growing" next to yellow dashed circles, and its dimples appear larger and deeper than those in (b).
Panel (f) shows blue dashed outlines around large dimple/quasi-cleavage regions at a 25 µm scale bar, but the annotation text associated with these outlines cannot be read.
No numeric axes or data values appear in any panel; the only printed quantitative anchors are the scale bar lengths 1 mm, 100 µm and 25 µm.
The caption states that (b, c) and (e, f) are microscopic features taken from the regions indicated by the arrows in (a) and (d), respectively.
The caption identifies (a) as the macroscopic fracture surface of the 0Al steel and (d) as the macroscopic fracture surface of the 1.3Al steel.

The citing text reports calculated shear fracture areas of 36.8 % for the 0Al steel and 42.9 % for the 1.3Al steel, based on the outlined regions of Fig. 8(a) and (d); these percentages are not printed in the image.

The citing text states that both the 0Al and 1.3Al steels exhibited pronounced shear lips and that numerous dimples near the crack initiation sites indicate ductile fracture via void growth and coalescence.

The citing text states that compared with (b), panel (e) shows a notable increase in the number and size of primary dimples, more prominent tearing ridges and greater overall surface roughness, indicating a higher density of large and deep dimples in the 1.3Al steel.
The citing text states that the notch region and initial fracture zone of the 1.3Al steel displayed significant plastic deformation, consistent with the fractographic evidence in this figure.
